title: Anti-money-laundering programme obligations for covered financial institutions
definition: The obligation on a covered financial institution to maintain a written, board-approved anti-money-laundering programme that is appropriate to the size and complexity of the institution. The programme is expected to contain a risk assessment, effective internal controls, a designated compliance officer, training, and independent testing, and to be revised when the institution's risks change. This record summarises the requirement; it is not the text of the rule.
evidence_to_cite: the institution's written anti-money-laundering programme and its approval date
the risk assessment the programme rests on, and its most recent review
the testing or independent review that the programme has been through

sources.citation: Anti-money-laundering programme requirements for banks (31 CFR 1020.210) and for money services businesses (31 CFR 1020.220), summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: A programme that exists but has not been revised since the institution's business or risk changed does not satisfy the requirement in substance.
